journey.name: Pubky links — share a profile or deck, open one back
journey.description:
The round trip a shared address makes. Loopky hands out `https://loopky.app` links from the share buttons on both profiles and on a deck (`/deck/?author=…&id=…`, `/profile/?pubky=…`), and still opens the `pubky://` URIs older shares carry; this journey checks that tapping either, or sharing the message that carries it back into Loopky, lands on the screen it names.
Until the Play signing fingerprint is in the landing site's assetlinks.json, the https link is unverified and Android 12+ opens it in the browser, so these steps pin the package with `-p`. `adb shell pm get-app-links com.github.jvsena42.loopky` shows the verification state.
Needs a signed-in session (journey 01), one published deck (journey 02) and, for the foreign half, one account you follow (journey 04). Deck ids appear in logcat as `Loopky/DeckDetailVM: load: deckId=…`; your own pubky is on the Profile tab's chip.
Most chat clients do not linkify an unknown scheme, so both intake paths matter: ACTION_VIEW for the ones that do, ACTION_SEND for the far more common paste-and-share.

actions.action: Launch the Loopky app and verify the Home screen is shown
Send a profile link with `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "pubky://<their-pubky>"` and verify their profile opens (resource-id: friend_profile_screen)
Verify the profile carries a Follow control (resource-id: friend_profile_follow), a Copy button (resource-id: friend_profile_copy) and a Share button (resource-id: friend_profile_share)

Verify a People card is shown with Following (resource-id: friend_profile_stat_following) and Followers (resource-id: friend_profile_stat_followers) counts. A dash while the follow graph resolves is a pass; a 0 that never resolves is not — the counts stay unset rather than reading as zero.

Tap the element with resource-id "friend_profile_stat_following" and verify their Following list opens. Its empty copy must NOT address you in the second person ("people you follow") — this is someone else's graph.
Navigate back, then press back again and verify the app returns to Home rather than exiting — a deep link opens on top of the tabs, not instead of them
Send your OWN profile link the same way and verify it opens with a "You" badge, no Follow button, and the Copy and Share buttons centered on their own row

Send a deck link with `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -d "pubky://<author>/pub/loopky/decks/<deckId>/manifest.json"` and verify the deck detail screen opens for that deck. Use a deck by someone else: the author travels with the link, so it must resolve on a cold cache.

Send the web form of a profile link: `adb shell am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -c android.intent.category.BROWSABLE -p com.github.jvsena42.loopky -d "'https://loopky.app/profile/?pubky=<their-pubky>'"` and verify the same profile opens
Send the web form of a deck link: `-d "'https://loopky.app/deck/?author=<author>&id=<deckId>'"` and verify the deck detail screen opens for that deck
Force-stop the app, send a profile link again, and verify the app cold-starts, restores the session, and still lands on that profile — the link is held until onboarding is past, not dropped
Open your own profile from the Profile tab and tap the Share button
Verify the share sheet (resource-id: share_link_uri) and the system share message carry an `https://loopky.app/profile/?pubky=…` link, not a bare key or a `pubky://` URI
Open a deck and tap the element with resource-id "deck_share"; verify the link reads `https://loopky.app/deck/?author=…&id=…`
Pick Loopky from that share sheet and verify it opens the profile the message points at — this is the ACTION_SEND path a chat client leaves as plain text
Send text with no address in it: `adb shell "am start -a android.intent.action.SEND -t text/plain -e android.intent.extra.TEXT 'definitely not a link' -n com.github.jvsena42.loopky/.MainActivity"`
Verify a toast says no Loopky link was found, rather than the app opening silently on whatever screen was already there
Tap the element with resource-id "tab_discover", then "discover_search"

Paste a DECK link into the element with resource-id "search_input" and tap the direct-hit row (resource-id: search_direct_hit), which must read "Open this deck". Verify the deck opens — not its author's profile (regression: the intake used to slice the URI by hand and could only reach people).

Go back to search, type free text with no address ("just some text") and verify it is treated as a QUERY — a people/deck search or the no-matches block (resource-id: search_empty) — with no direct-hit row offered
Go back to search, paste the whole shared message — greeting line and address together — and verify the direct-hit row still resolves the right screen
